source.title: Countering Noisy Labels By Learning From Auxiliary Clean Labels
source.authors: Tsung Wei Tsai; Chong-Xuan Li; Jun Zhu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study varies synthetic label-noise levels and reports test accuracy, bearing on the test-error part of V4. It does not measure whether training error remains zero or near zero.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own test accuracies under synthetic label noise in Table 1. Table 2 comparisons are excluded because they are results from the literature, not this study's own results. No own result tests fitting completely random labels, unstructured inputs, regularization effects on fitting random labels, or learning order.
record.test_reason: The study uses neural networks' capacity to memorize noise to motivate a mitigation method, then measures generalization and pseudo-label quality. It does not measure training-label fit, optimization difficulty, or learning order. Test-accuracy degradation alone does not establish V4's joint claim of perfect training fit and worsening generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that RDCR achieves comparable or superior generalization across tested noise settings, with especially large gains under heavy noise, and improves semi-supervised performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains consistency-based models with an added rotation self-supervision task and, in its main setup, GN+WS normalization; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and symmetric-noise level change the reported test accuracy; the paper also evaluates asymmetric noise at 40%.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports declining final test accuracy with increasing symmetric noise, and improved robustness from RDCR. For CIFAR-10, CE accuracy falls from 84.04% at 20% noise to 25.15% at 80%; RD-MT falls from 94.17% to 84.00%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary rotation supervision improves generalization under synthetic label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 measures training-set pseudo-label agreement with true labels at 80% symmetric noise. RD-MT produces cleaner pseudo labels than MT. The authors interpret MT's confusion pattern as memorization, but do not report agreement with observed noisy labels or near-zero training error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary rotation supervision improves pseudo-label correction under heavy label noise.

record.problems: For the claim's training-fit behavior, the paper reports no training-error measurements and does not test 100% random labels. Table 1 gives test accuracy only. The text does not give uncertainty for Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows retained: Table 1 reports test accuracy across noise levels but does not measure the training-fit behavior required by V4; the other versions are not tested. Table 2 results are literature comparisons and were excluded.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error and chance test performance on completely random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time required to fit random versus real labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian inputs.

Perfect training fit across corruption levels, paired with steadily worsening test performance through fully random labeling. Test accuracy is reported at selected noise levels, but training error is not.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing them.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels. Best-versus-final test accuracy does not measure this learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate for these claim versions. Correct the record's blanket description of Table 2: it includes the authors' own RD-MT and RD-fast-SWA results alongside literature comparisons. Neither those results nor the other mitigation comparisons establish a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random training labels to zero or near-zero training error, test at chance, and do so without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence speed as corruption grows.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

The study reports test accuracy under several synthetic noise levels, but does not report training error, test error through all corruption levels from none to all, or evidence that the model captures remaining signal while memorizing noise.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect fitting random labels, and whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
